newsitem.title: USA: California bill could break up Los Angeles County.
newsitem.headline: California bill could break up Los Angeles County.

text.p: A California state legislator on Friday proposed a measure that could lead to the break-up of Los Angeles County into two or more separate government entities.
"We believe that Los Angeles County is too large to operate effectively," Republican state Assemblyman George Runner said in a statement.
Los Angeles County has over nine million residents and is comprised of 88 cities.
Runner's Assembly Bill 303 would create a local agency known as the Los Angeles County Revision Authority. The authority would be made up of representatives of local jurisdictions in the county.
The purpose of the authority would be to determine if the division of Los Angeles County into two or more smaller counties would improve local finances and service delivery.
"The diverse needs of the residents and cities within the county require this special study to determine how best to provide governmental services," Runner said.
